2. Heard Sri Ripu Soodan Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Bare Lal Bind, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.
3. Learned counsel for the States submits that he has received instructions in the matter for which time was granted on 18.8.2023.

4. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Manoj Saroj, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No.
149 of 2023, under Section 366, 376 I.P.C., registered at P.S. Sandeepan Ghat, District Kaushambi.

sentences.text: The F.I.R. of the matter was lodged on 23.6.2023 under Sections 366, 376 I.P.C. by the victim herself against the applicant alleging therein that on 20.6.2023 at about 3.00 pm the applicant allured her and enticed her away.
She took Rs.20,000/- and jewellery from her house while going.
He took her to an orchard where he committed rape on her and left her at Bharwari Railway Station.
She came back to her house and then the F.I.R. has been lodged.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that as per X-ray examination report the victim has been opined to be aged about 20-25 years.
It is argued that on the own showing of the victim, she went from the house after taking Rs.20,000/- and jewellery which would go to show that she went from the house out of her own sweet will.
It is argued that the victim is a major woman and the present case is a case of consent.
It is argued that the applicant has no other criminal antecedents as stated in para-17 of the affidavit and is in jail since 27.6.2023.
7. Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments as aforesaid.

8. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that as per X-ray examination report she has been opined to be aged about 20-25 years and as such she is major.
She herself states that she went from the house after taking Rs.20,000/- and jewellery.

9. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

10. Let the applicant- Manoj Saroj, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court Manoj Saroj vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96264839/
2 shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(V) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.
( vi )
The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.

11. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
12. The bail application is allowed.
(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 19.9.2023
